facts.statement: Elsornis is classified as a genus of enantiornithean bird.
facts.quote: Elsornis is a genus of enantiornithean bird.

facts.statement: Only one species, Elsornis keni, has been named within the genus Elsornis.
facts.quote: Only one species has been named, Elsornis keni.

facts.statement: Elsornis lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: It lived during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil of Elsornis carries the catalogue number MPD-b 100/201.
facts.quote: The holotype fossil has been given the catalogue number MPD - b 100/201.

facts.statement: The fossil was collected at Togrogiin Shiree in the Djadokhta Formation, dating to the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The fossil was collected at Togrogiin Shiree, South Gobi Aimak, Mongolia; Djadokhta Formation, Late Cretaceous, Campanian.

facts.statement: The fossil skeleton is extremely well preserved in three dimensions.
facts.quote: The fossil is extremely well preserved in three dimensions.

facts.statement: The fossil preserves a pneumatized furcula, a feature previously unknown in enantiornitheans.
facts.quote: It preserves a pneumatized Furcula, which was a character previously unknown in enantiornitheans.

facts.statement: Researchers Chiappe et al. (2007) concluded that Elsornis was flightless or nearly so based on its pectoral skeleton proportions.
facts.quote: Chiappe et al. (2007) conclude from the proportions of Elsornis ' pectoral skeleton that it was flightless or nearly so.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that Elsornis may have glided like Archaeopteryx to pounce on ground prey.
facts.quote: It may have glided like Archaeopteryx, climbing in trees to pounce on its prey on the ground.

facts.statement: Alternatively, Elsornis may have hunted on the ground by snatching small vertebrates and insects.
facts.quote: However, if this is not the case, it may have hunted on the ground, snatching up small vertebrates and bugs.

facts.statement: Elsornis likely possessed small, non-serrated teeth for hunting and possibly scavenged carcasses left by larger carnivores.
facts.quote: Like the other members of Avisauridae, it probably had small non-serrated teeth it used for hunting, and possibly scavenged the carcasses left by other, more formidable carnivores.

facts.statement: A 2018 study by Atterholt et al. places Elsornis in the family Avisauridae.
facts.quote: A study by Atterholt et al. in 2018 places Elsornis in the family Avisauridae.

facts.statement: The genus name Elsornis combines the Mongolian word for sand and the Greek word for bird.
facts.quote: The genus name Elsornis is derived from the Mongolian word "els", meaning "sand", and "ornis", the Greek word for "bird".

facts.statement: The species name keni honors Mr. Ken Hayashibara.
facts.quote: The specific name "keni" honors Mr. Ken Hayashibara.

facts.statement: Elsornis lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Elsornis is known from a partially articulated fossil skeleton discovered in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia.
rejected.quote: It is known from a partially articulated fossil skeleton found in the Gobi Desert in Mongolia.
